name: Minutes-November 5, 2019
minutes_text:
Final Minutes Approved November 19, 2019

  Regular Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Tuesday, November 5, 2019

Sergeant at Arms read the Rules of Decorum before the start of the Regular Meeting.

The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
called to order at 6:02 p.m. on Tuesday, November 5, 2019, in the Council Chambers at
City Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Karina Macias
presiding.

PRESENT: Council Member(s): Graciela Ortiz, Jhonny Pineda, Marilyn Sanabria, Vice
Mayor Manuel "Manny" Avila and Mayor Karina Macias.

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: Ricardo Reyes, City Manager; Raul Alvarez, Assistant City
Manager; Noel Tapia, Assistant City Attorney; Cosme Lozano, Chief of Police; Cynthia
Norzagaray, Director of Parks and Recreation; Nita McKay, Director of Finance &
Administrative Services; Sergio lnfanzon, Director of Community Development and
Donna G. Schwartz, City Clerk.

INVOCATION

The invocation was led by Mayor Macias.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Sara Hernandez.

PRESENTATIONS

Council presented "Certificates of Appreciation," to Sara Hernandez for leading the
Pledge of Allegiance.

Council presented a "Certificate of Recognition," to Ms. Moreno Aria, Miles Elementary
School Teacher, for receiving 'Teacher of the Year."

Council presented "Certificates of Recognition," to Dedicated Parent and Teacher
Volunteers.

Council presented "Certificates of Recognition," to those who Volunteered at the Health
and Education Commission's First Annual Book Fair held Saturday, June 1, 2019 at Salt
Lake Park.

Council presented a proclamation to the Huntington Park Kiwanis Club proclaiming
November 4-8, 2019, as "National Key Club Week" and recognized various Key Club
Members from the local high schools.

PUBLIC COMMENT

1.  Leticia Martinez, spoke in support of the efforts by the American Cancer Society
  working with District 9 Council to ban flavored tobacco and sales and asked the
  City to do the same.

STAFF RESPONSE - None.

CLOSED SESSION

At 7:07 p.m. Noel Tapia, Assistant City Attorney, recessed to closed session.

  1. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS Regarding Represented
  Employees - Government Code Section 54957.6(a)
  City's Designated Representative(s) for Negotiations: Ricardo Reyes, City
  Manager and Nita McKay, Finance/Administrative Services Director
  Employee Organization: General Employees Association (GEA)
 CLOSED SESSION (CONTINUED)

  2. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR - Regarding Represented
  Employees
  (Government Code Section 54957.6(a))
  City's Designated Representative(s) for Negotiations: Ricardo Reyes, City
  Manager
  Employee Organization: Police Officers Association (POA)

At 7:52 p.m. Mayor Macias reconvened to open session with all Council Members present.

CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

Noel Tapia, Assistant City Attorney, announced all Council Members were present and
briefed on closed session items 1 and 2. 1.) directions was given, no action taken, nothing
to report. 2.) direction was given, no action taken, nothing to report.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion: Council Member Ortiz moved to approve consent calendar, seconded by
Council Member Sanabria. Motion passed 5-0, by the following vote:

  Mayor Macias

OFFICE OF THE CITY CLERK

1.  Approved Minute(s) of the following City Council Meeting(s):

  1-1.  Regular City Council Meeting held October 15, 2019.

FINANCE

4.  Council Appointment to Youth Commission

City Manager Ricardo Reyes announced the Item.

Motion: Mayor Macias moved to appoint Johanna Ramos to the Youth Commission,
term will run concurrent with Mayor's term ending 2022.

CITY MANAGER

5.  Consideration and Approval to Enter into an Agreement with Pacific Media

City Manager Ricardo Reyes presented the staff report.

Motion: Council Member Ortiz moved to approve the public-private partnership
agreement with Pacific Media for the construction of Billboards on City Premises and
authorize City Manager to execute and negotiate final terms of agreement, seconded by
Mayor Macias. Motion passed 5-0, by the following vote:

Council Member Sanabria. Motion passed 4-0-1, by the following vote:

City Manager Ricardo Reyes announced the Item.

Motion: Council Member Ortiz moved to waive first reading and introduce Ordinance No.

Limited", Chapter 7 "Traffic", Title 4 "Public Safety" of the City of Huntington Park's
Municipal Code Relating to Parking of Vehicles for Sale and schedule the second reading

9.  Consideration and Approval to Appropriate Funds for the Purchase and
  Replacement of two Police Department Main Information Technology
  Servers

City Manager Ricardo Reyes announced the Item.

Motion: Council Member Ortiz moved to approve an appropriation transfer in the amount
of $146,730.00 to be transferred to account number 111-7010-421.74-10 Police
Department Capital Outlay - Equipment from account number 111-6010-451.73-10 City­
Wide Park Improvements in the amount of $125,000 and 111-6010-451-74-1 O Parks and
Recreation Capital Outlay - Equipment in the amount of $21,730, authorize the Director
of Finance & Administrative Services to issue a purchase order in the amount of
$146,730.00 to be expended for the replacement of two police department main
information technology servers and associated software and licensing upgrades,
authorize the services of LAN WAN to install the new servers and configure software
upgrades and authorize the Chief of Police to complete this project, seconded
Council Member Sanabria. Motion passed 5-0, by the following vote:

ROLL CALL:

  Mayor Macias

13.  Consideration and Approval to Enter into an Agreement with Los Angeles
  County to Make the Necessary Pavement Improvements on Mountain View
  Avenue Between Walnut Street and Florence Avenue and Walnut Street
  Between Mountain View Avenue and State Street

City Manager Ricardo Reyes announced the Item.

Motion: Vice Mayor Avila moved to approve and authorize the Mayor to sign the
cooperative agreement between the City and Los Angeles County to finance and delegate
responsibilities for the design, construction and management of the portion of the
roadway improvements on Mountain View Avenue between Walnut Street and Florence
Avenue and Walnut Street between Mountain View Avenue and State Street, seconded
by Council Member Sanabria. Motion passed 5-0, by the following vote:

  Mayor

  END OF REGULAR AGENDA

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS (Information only)

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - None.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Council Member Graciela Ortiz, thanked everyone and wished all a good night.

Council Member Jhonny Pineda, commented on calls he's received regarding parking on
streets and asked to either put T-marks or more parking enforcement but for staff to look
for a solution, pointed out trash and big trucks being an issue around HP High School,
trash on major street and asked staff to be aware, thanked staff for their support and
wished all a good night.

Council Member Marilyn Sanabria, thanked staff for their support, acknowledge how great
the Halloween Festival and the Dia de Los Muertos Events were, thanked her colleagues
and wished all a good night.

Vice Mayor Manuel "Manny" Avila, wished everyone a good night.

Mayor Karina Macias, thanked staff for all their support with the Halloween Festival noting
she is hearing good things about it, thanked staff for the Dia de Los Muertos Event and
asked permission from her colleagues if the City Seal can be used by ARP for an
upcoming care givers event, Council concurred their approval.

ADJOURNMENT

At 8:15 p.m. Mayor Macias adjourned the City of Huntington Park City Council in memory
of Elijah Cummings an American politician and civil rights advocate to a Regular Meeting
on Tuesday, November 19, 2019 at 6:00 P.M.
